// Windows only file
//
// To streamline your WindowsNativeInputHandler class using Microsoft's CsWin32 source generator, you need to create a NativeMethods.txt file and update your class to use the auto-generated P/Invoke methods, structs, and constants.
// Format of NativeMethods.txt
// The NativeMethods.txt file is a simple, line-by-line configuration file placed at the root of your project. Each line can contain one of the following:
//
//     An exported method name: e.g., SetWindowLongPtr.
//
//     A macro or constant name: e.g., WM_ERASEBKGND.
//
//     A namespace: e.g., Windows.Win32.UI.WindowsAndMessaging (generates all APIs in it).
//
//     A module with a wildcard: e.g., User32.* (generates everything from User32.dll).
//
//     A specific type name: e.g., RECT or WNDPROC.
//
//     A comment: Starts with //. Blank lines are also ignored.
//
// Customization of the generated code is found in the `NativeMethods.json` file
//

// Window setup and message handling
SetWindowLong
SetWindowLongPtr
CallWindowProc
GetClientRect
DefWindowProc

CreateSolidBrush

VK_SHIFT

// Mouse Capturing: Cursor movement message is emitted only if a mouse moves within the window itself. If movement goes outside the window,
// the window stops receivim messages. That means that the window needs to capture the mouse. Furthermore, if we want to replicate a "dragging"
// functionality, wParam stores the window button being pressed
SetCapture
ReleaseCapture
SetCursorPos
